question.text: Cash-flow matching (as a passive FI strategy) differs from immunization in that it:

answer.text: Matches each future cash flow to a corresponding coupon/principal payment
Uses derivatives to hedge interest rate risk

explanation.text: The Logic: Cash-flow matching (dedication) builds a portfolio whose individual coupon and principal payments coincide with each liability payment date. Because each future cash inflow is explicitly funded by a corresponding bond payment, reinvestment risk is largely eliminated across the entire liability schedule, not only at a single horizon date. The Trap: Matching only duration to the liability horizon defines immunization, not cash-flow matching. Using derivatives is derivative-based hedging, and rotating between sectors is an active strategy — neither qualifies as a passive cash-flow matching approach. Note: The Portfolio Managers (NISM-Series-XXI-B) workbook lists passive strategies such as buy-and-hold, indexing, and immunization (including matching portfolio duration to the liability time frame), but does not explicitly describe cash-flow matching / dedicated portfolios that fund each liability payment. The distinction above reflects general industry/regulatory fixed-income strategy terminology.
